title: Moscow, November 5 - Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council made remarks in an interview.
text:
Moscow, November 5 - Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council made remarks in an interview."

"———-"

"SOT1, Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council (Farsi) (00:00 - 00:31): “I was the messenger of the Supreme Leader of Iran for Mr. Putin. Of course, this trip was supposed to take place about a month ago, but it was delayed due to special circumstances, as discussions regarding the military situation in the region were being raised every day. The Supreme Leader wished for me to present his message to His Excellency Mr. Putin, the honorable President of the Russian Federation, as soon as possible.”"

"SOT2, Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council (Farsi) (00:32 - 01:06): “We consulted with him [ Mr. Putin] regarding important issues we have in the region. Currently, important discussions are being raised regarding the post-war period, especially concerning regional security arrangements. I submitted a report on the four-country meeting in Tehran, and he welcomed it. He stated that, like our Chinese friends, we believe there should be regional arrangements in place and that foreign countries should not interfere in the security of the region.”"

""
"SOT3, Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council (Farsi) (01:07 - 01:48): “The issue of the Rasht-Astara corridor was discussed, which fortunately the Supreme National Security Council approved, and our Minister of Roads will soon implement this contract following the signing. Discussions regarding the construction of gas pipelines from Russia to Iran, which would both address Iran’s own gas shortages and allow us to sell Russian gas to the countries surrounding Iran, were very important discussions regarding our future relations with Mr. Vladimir Putin.”"

"SOT4, Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council (Farsi) (01:49 - 02:46): “Regarding military matters, he strongly and firmly condemned the military attacks by the United States and Israel against Iran. He condemned the bombing of Iran’s nuclear sites and believed that this was an unjust war that must end as quickly as possible. He stated that we are ready to provide any assistance possible to help end the war. However, we informed them that regarding the diplomacy, we have declared seven conditions to the Americans, and until the Americans fulfill our seven conditions, neither the Strait of Hormuz will be opened nor will there be any negotiations. title: **Yazd Commemorates 13 Aban With Tribute to Minab Children Killed in Missile Strikes**
text:
**Yazd Commemorates 13 Aban With Tribute to Minab Children Killed in Missile Strikes**"

"**YAZD, Iran —** A commemorative event in the central Iranian city of Yazd marked 13 Aban by honoring children from Minab, a city in southern Iran, who were killed in missile strikes, with organizers invoking “dreams left unfinished beneath the rubble of missiles.”"

"The tribute combined Iran’s annual 13 Aban commemorations with a memorial for young victims from Minab. The Persian-language headline is feature-style and emphasizes the loss of children’s futures rather than providing detailed news reporting."

"**Background for international readers:** 13 Aban falls in late October or early November on the Iranian calendar and is observed in Iran as “Student Day” and the “National Day of Fight Against Global Arrogance.”"

" It commemorates a 1978 confrontation between students and security forces in Tehran and the 1979 seizure of the U.S. Embassy. Commemorations often mix historical remembrance with current political messaging. Minab is located in Hormozgan Province in southern Iran.

title: 🔆🔅November 4th - An important message from the Supreme Leader of Iran, Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Khamenei marking the National Day of Combating Global Arrogance, read by TV presenter.
text:
🔆🔅November 4th - An important message from the Supreme Leader of Iran, Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Khamenei marking the National Day of Combating Global Arrogance, read by TV presenter."

""
"========"

" "Now, the story of America's longstanding enmity toward the Muslim nation of Iran, and the courageous resistance of all Iranians against this enemy, has reached a point where not only November 4, but every day and every hour, has become a time of steadfastness and struggle against the Great Satan.""

""Now, the situation in the Persian Gulf, particularly in the Strait of Hormuz, has exposed the falsehood of the myth of America's invincibility. It demonstrates the weakness and humiliation of governments that rely on powers other than their own people, as well as the disloyalty and inability of major powers to defend their puppet regimes. Iran's management of the Strait of Hormuz and the destruction of US military bases in countries across the region, although a response to US aggression and crimes during the Third Imposed War, also constituted an initial offensive jihad against global arrogance on a regional scale. Should these acts of aggression be repeated, it will take on much broader dimensions.""

" "This display of strength, alongside the unity of the various arenas of the Front of Truth and the intelligent and powerful acts of heroism by the Resistance Front, from Palestine and Lebanon to Iraq and Yemen, is a bright and hopeful harbinger of the rising flag of the Front of Truth and the groundwork being laid for a new global order. For whenever the Front of Truth is armed with reliance on God, steadfastness, and self-sacrifice, the Front of Falsehood, whatever its power or capabilities, and whoever or whatever it may be, will be unable to withstand it. Retreat and defeat will be its inevitable fate.""

""Today, as a result of the arrogant powers' self-inflicted disgrace, America's declining power and hegemony have suffered an irreversible collapse in both dimensions of hard military power and international soft power, and the process of its disintegration has accelerated.""

" "If there are still those who hold even the slightest hope for a change in behavior or partisan and factional shifts within the system of hegemony, or who imagine that by granting concessions to America they can dissuade it from its hostility toward the Iranian nation, they are gravely mistaken. This mistaken belief is an expression of ingratitude toward the great victories that the Muslim nation of Iran has achieved through reliance on God, steadfastness, and struggle.""

""The wish of the Great Satan is the unconditional surrender of the Iranian nation. Even the slightest inclination toward surrender to the hegemonic enemy would squander the immense capital gained through the blood of the martyrs and the sacrifices of the people, and would embolden the arrogant enemy to pursue further demands, wage further wars, and commit further acts of aggression.

title: 🔅🔅TEHRAN, NOVEMBER 4 – Mohammad Javad Larijani, senior expert on international affairs and head of the Institute for Research in Fundamental Sciences, said the Iranian people have a serious demand for a change in the country's nuclear doctrine in an interview with Fars News Agency.
text:
🔅🔅TEHRAN, NOVEMBER 4 – Mohammad Javad Larijani, senior expert on international affairs and head of the Institute for Research in Fundamental Sciences, said the Iranian people have a serious demand for a change in the country's nuclear doctrine in an interview with Fars News Agency."

""
"========="

"SOT1, Mohammad Javad Larijani, a senior expert on international affairs (Farsi) (00:00 - 00:41): "We are a member of the NPT and, in accordance with our commitments, have not pursued nuclear weapons and will not do so as long as we remain a member. The fatwa issued by our martyred Imam [Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei] also prohibited weapons of mass destruction, including chemical and nuclear weapons. However, our membership in the NPT has brought us no benefits, only disadvantages. In my view, Parliament should quickly withdraw from its practical commitments under the NPT. Then let them argue with us. If they insist that we remain a member of the NPT, why should we?""

"SOT2, Mohammad Javad Larijani, a senior expert on international affairs (Farsi) (00:42 - 01:37): "How much would possessing nuclear weapons actually contribute to deterrence within our defense doctrine? This is a very important issue, and people have a serious demand on this matter as well. God willing, officials will pay attention to it. We must consider the Supreme Leader's final position, as this is ultimately a matter for him to decide. However, nuclear knowledge and technology extend far beyond simply building a bomb; building a bomb is easy compared with acquiring the knowledge behind it. The enemy wants us to lose that knowledge. My objection is also to entering negotiations in a way that focuses on our scientific and technological capabilities. As for discussing whether we should remain in or withdraw from the NPT, that is a separate matter.

Under these circumstances, dialogue and negotiation should be viewed from this perspective. Ultimately, we can neither forget nor ignore the past or the events that have occurred over these two years; however, we have always stated that we have no fear of diplomacy. The point is that our logic is clear, our reasoning is clear, and we know we are in the right. From this angle, we use the tools of diplomacy and dialogue to secure the interests of the Iranian people and, simultaneously, to prevent the escalation of insecurity in the region.”"

We do not need to go far back into the past; look at the events that have occurred within this past year. In less than one year, on two separate occasions while we were in the middle of negotiations, they attacked Iran; subsequently, when the Islamabad understanding was reached, less than two or three weeks later, the U.S. [acted differently]. With full knowledge of this experience, and to speak without reservation and with the utmost caution, we participated in every diplomatic process with complete skepticism.”"

""

As long as our demands are completely legitimate and logical, we cannot talk about the content of Iran’s demands. What was agreed upon in the Islamabad understanding and unfortunately violated by the Americans,in clause one of the understanding, the issue of halting the war on all fronts, including Lebanon, this is one of the key issues of any diplomatic process.”

"Close doors and windows and turn off ventilation systems that draw in outside air."

title: IRGC Claims It Has Downed 68 US MQ-1 and MQ-9 Drones in the Strait of Hormuz Area
text:
IRGC Claims It Has Downed 68 US MQ-1 and MQ-9 Drones in the Strait of Hormuz Area"

"Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has released images said to show the interception and destruction of advanced US-made MQ-1 and MQ-9 drones over the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC said the footage includes the interception and downing of one MQ-1 early on Thursday, 29 October, east of the Strait of Hormuz, off the coast of Sirik."

"According to the IRGC Public Relations Office, the MQ-1 downed that morning brings the total number of these two specific types of US drones destroyed by the IRGC Aerospace Force’s new advanced air defense system to 68 — including 54 MQ-9s and 14 MQ-1s."

"The IRGC said the system operates under Iran’s integrated air defense network and has been used against drones that it describes as among the United States’ valuable reconnaissance and combat assets. It said the significance of the claimed achievement is not only the number of drones destroyed, but also the ability to detect, track and destroy advanced targets under real combat conditions, a capability it says is the result of years of work by Iranian specialists and commanders in developing indigenous air defense."

"Source: IRGC Public Relations Office.

"SOT1, Ali Bagheri Kani, Deputy Secretary for the Supreme National Security Council of Iran (Farsi)-(00:00 - 00:27): “Today’s four-party meeting in Tehran can effectively be described as a fruit of the heroic resistance of the Iranian people and the victorious valor of the Armed Forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran. It led these countries to a common conclusion, even though their priorities and approaches may differ significantly.”"

"SOT2, Ali Bagheri Kani, Deputy Secretary for the Supreme National Security Council of Iran (Farsi)-(00:28 - 00:46): “The Tehran session in fact conveyed a message: even if we have differences and disagreements, through dialogue we can reach a point where we embark on a path that produces solutions for us and can even become a source of cooperation.”"

"SOT3, Ali Bagheri Kani, Deputy Secretary for the Supreme National Security Council of Iran (Farsi)-(00:47 - 01:09): “The fundamental discussion held today,which in fact centered on several discussions concerning the fortification of security, is a crucial foundational issue. If we can truly establish sustainable security, it can serve as the basis for development and progress. However, if security is not sustainable, development will not actually take shape; and even if development does occur, it will not be sustainable.”"

"SOT4, Ali Bagheri Kani, Deputy Secretary for the Supreme National Security Council of Iran (Farsi)-(01:10 - 01:53): “For years, the Islamic Republic of Iran has emphasized this point: Neighboring countries, brothers! if we truly want to live in a secure region characterized by prosperity and progress, we must engage in synergistic interaction. It is not possible for one country in the region to have security while another does not; security is an interconnected principle. Therefore, when external countries intervene, since they fundamentally seek to secure their own interests, it is not necessarily the case that securing Country A will also secure Country B. Sometimes they enter the region specifically to jeopardize the security of Country B.”"

"SOT5, Ali Bagheri Kani, Deputy Secretary for the Supreme National Security Council of Iran (Farsi)-( 01:54 - 02:38): “Another noteworthy point for me at the Tehran meeting was that all four parties were motivated by the intention of being able to create a path for cooperation. That is, it was not a case in which one country insisted on its own perspective and wanted the others eventually to be dragged along that path. Rather, it was about creating a framework, a framework that could attract the cooperation of these four countries as a core and as an origin for other countries in the region, so that they too would participate in the process of security-making in the region.”

"**Tehran, October 23, 2026** — A friendly cricket match between the Iran Cricket Association and a team representing the Indian Embassy was held at Velayat Park in southern Tehran on Friday, offering a glimpse of efforts to expand the sport’s presence in Iran through international sporting exchanges."

"The match comes amid a series of recent contacts between Iran’s cricket authorities and South Asian partners. In August, the Pakistan Cricket Board held talks with an Iranian delegation on coaching support, player development, infrastructure and equipment. In September, the Bangladeshi Embassy in Tehran also reported discussions with the head of the Iran Cricket Association on strengthening cooperation in cricket."

"Cricket remains a relatively niche sport in Iran. The International Cricket Council notes that the game has traditionally had a stronger presence among expatriates in Tehran, while activity has also grown in southern regions bordering Pakistan."

"Against this background, friendly matches and sporting exchanges could provide opportunities to build contacts, share expertise and attract new participants. The Tehran match, however, was a friendly fixture, not an official international competition."

"**Potential focus:** Can sporting exchanges with India, Pakistan and Bangladesh help Iran build a broader domestic cricket base?

title: Qatar Must Account for Iranian Pilots; They Are “Alive”
text:
Qatar Must Account for Iranian Pilots; They Are “Alive”"

"🔆🔅TEHRAN — October 20, 2026 — The Iranian Army’s deputy chief for legal and parliamentary affairs said the Qatari government must account for the Iranian pilots, stating that Iran considers them “alive” and that Qatar bears “international responsibility.”"

""
"SOT1, Moslem Yaqoubi, Deputy for Legal and Parliamentary Affairs of the Army of the Islamic Republic of Iran(Farsi)-(00:00 - 00:55): "According to documents, evidence, and the Qatari government’s contradictory claims, legally speaking, our presumption is that the pilots are alive. In other words, the principle is that they are alive, because no proof of their martyrdom, or, rather, of their not being alive, has been presented. This is a legal principle, and in our jurisprudence (fiqh) we also have the rule of presumption of continuity, which means maintaining a situation that previously existed. They set out alive and carried out a mission. Our opposing party in this conflict was the Qatari government, of course, Qatar itself was not the opposing party; the American bases located there were the opposing party. But even if a strike occurred, it occurred in the airspace surrounding the Qatari government, and Qatar’s international responsibility remains in place.""

"SOT2, Moslem Yaqoubi, Deputy for Legal and Parliamentary Affairs of the Army of the Islamic Republic of Iran(Farsi)-(00:56 - 01:25): "Basically, under international law, the state hosting the prisoners is responsible for locating them alive, providing medical treatment, giving information to their families, and ultimately handing them over to the competent authorities, whether the Red Cross, a protecting power, or the government of the prisoners’ nationality. In fact, this is an obligation of governments under the Geneva Quartet Conventions.""

"SOT3, Moslem Yaqoubi, Deputy for Legal and Parliamentary Affairs of the Army of the Islamic Republic of Iran(Farsi)-(01:26 - 02:18): "The Geneva Quartet Conventions provide for a specific legal follow-up system; that is, we recognize the International Red Cross as a neutral and supporting organization responsible for follow-up. We have conveyed official correspondence, requests for official visits, and demands to the Qatari government, even at the level of heads of state, and we have reminded it of the Qatari government’s international responsibility. This is because, as you are aware, in the field of international law it is international responsibility that keeps states bound. It is our presumption that they are alive, except for that dear martyr whose body we actually received and whose martyrdom was confirmed to us through DNA testing.""

"SOT4, Moslem Yaqoubi: "We have concluded that their survival is presumed. The Qatari government has provided us with no evidence of their death or martyrdom, the Qatari government’s international responsibility remains in effect, and we are pursuing the matter through international authorities.

text:
🔆🔅Baghdad - Oct 18, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi made remarks on the sidelines of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) Council of Foreign Ministers. "

""

"SOT1: "Serious discussions took place regarding Yemen, in this meeting [of OIC], the Saudis expressed their views, we expressed ours, and other countries did the same. A resolution was requested to be passed in this regard, but it has not yet been finalized.""

"SOT2: "We hope that fairness and balance are maintained in this resolution and in the final statement concerning the summit. Naturally, if this does not happen, the Islamic Republic of Iran will not be able to join them, and we will certainly reserve our position, separating ourselves from the issued resolutions, including that specific resolution. We might even explicitly declare our non-acceptance, depending on what the text of the resolution is. Naturally, the bloc of countries within the Organization of Islamic Cooperation that are close to Saudi Arabia's positions is a significant bloc; this is a reality that we must take into consideration. We have, of course, conducted extensive lobbying, and in my speech, I clearly stated what the fair solution is, and we hope that it will be taken into account.""

"SOT3: " [at UNGA] In New York, we presented our seven-point, seven-item, seven-day plan [to the U.S]. Here, we emphasized diplomatic ways, and countries are interested in this, as this region can no longer tolerate more threats and conflicts. They are interested in finding a peaceful solution, and the Islamic Republic is a pioneer in this matter and has shown its will on this path. Therefore, we are moving forward with both approaches simultaneously. The international community must know, and does know, that the Islamic Republic of Iran is a proponent of diplomacy, logic, and dialogue; at the same time, it is also a proponent of battle and struggle. If it is subjected to aggression, it will defend itself with strength. There is no contradiction between these two.""

"SOT4: "Our conditions are completely clear and have been presented to the American side in the form of the seven-day plan. They have provided comments that we are currently reviewing, but from our perspective, this plan is still on the table. If there were true sincerity on the American side, which there isn't, the path would be wide open. The Strait of Hormuz has a very specific route; if they comply with those conditions, the strait will be opened on the sixth day, and negotiations will be held on the seventh day.""

"SOT5:  "The conditions we have set are not strange or unusual; I have said this before. They are all conditions to which the United States had previously committed itself in the prior memorandum of understanding and in other negotiations. They are completely fair conditions, and we believe that if the United States has the will, it can fulfill these conditions within a few days, and the Strait of Hormuz will then be opened.

title: Yerevan - Oct 16, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian made remarks durinng addressing the 17th Summit of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP 17).
text:
Yerevan - Oct 16, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian made remarks durinng addressing the 17th Summit of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP 17)."

""

"------"

"SOT1, Masoud Pezeshkian, President of Iran (Farsi) (00:00 - 00:38): "War does not only target humans and economic infrastructures; it also harms nature. It burns forests, destroys wetlands, contaminates the soil, threatens water resources, eradicates habitats, displaces animal species, and introduces chemicals and heavy metals into natural cycles. The effects of war on the environment can persist for years after the hostilities have ended.""

"SOT2, Masoud Pezeshkian, President of Iran (Farsi) (00:39 - 01:29): "Today, the international community knows well that environmental destruction in armed conflicts is not a secondary or insignificant consequence of war; these damages are directly linked to the security and well-being of future generations. In our region, including Iran, the environmental impacts of military conflicts must be addressed with greater seriousness by the global community. The war and the aggressive wars waged by the United States and the Zionist regime in our region, by damaging industrial and energy facilities, causing fires, emitting pollutants, and contaminating soil and water, have threatened natural ecosystems and destroyed protective infrastructures.""

""
"SOT3, Masoud Pezeshkian, President of Iran: "War-related damages are also issues of a global nature and require international solutions. The effects of war on ecosystems can persist for years or even generations, impacting areas many kilometers beyond the conflict zone. A clear testament to this is the scale of destruction recorded in oppressed Gaza; according to experts, parts of its soil will be unable to host life or natural ecological and botanical cycles for hundreds of years to come.""

""
"SOT4, Masoud Pezeshkian, President of Iran: "What has occurred in our region due to aggressive wars is ecocide, which must be condemned. The international community is expected to create effective, transparent, and enforceable mechanisms to protect natural heritage and biodiversity. No country should consider nature to be a silent and defenseless victim during times of war.""

""
"SOT5, Masoud Pezeshkian, President of Iran: "[Iran] A country that simultaneously faces pressures from climate change, drought, water scarcity, desertification, and the depletion of natural resources on one hand, and the effects of economic sanctions and limited access to technology and financial resources on the other; and which, for two consecutive years, has been the target of criminal wars involving the extensive use of destructive, prohibited weapons and, in many cases, with the deliberate aim of environmental destruction, such as attacks on fuel depots in the capital. To implement environmental programs and compensate for the damages incurred, it must benefit from genuine global cooperation.

title: Iran, 12 other delegations walk out at CICA Summit in Baku over Israeli PM speech
text:
Iran, 12 other delegations walk out at CICA Summit in Baku over Israeli PM speech "
" "
"🔆🔅BAKU, 15 Oct 2026 — The Iranian delegation to the 7th Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia (CICA), led by Kazem Gharibabadi, Deputy Foreign Minister for Legal and International Affairs, along with 12 other delegations, walked out of the summit hall on Thursday as the Israeli representative began his speech. "

"The walkout was in protest against the Israeli leader’s address. The delegations of Iran, Palestine, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Iraq, Egypt, Kuwait, Qatar, Jordan, Malaysia, Indonesia, and Bangladesh left the hall. "

text:

""
"=============="

"SOT1, Behrouz Kamalvandi, Spokesperson for the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran (Farsi)-(00:00 - 00:24): "What is important is that the world knows that Iran's nuclear program has been completely peaceful and transparent, under the constant supervision of the IAEA. Numerous IAEA reports have shown that Iran has always moved along the right path, maintaining a transparent yet highly advanced program.""

"SOT2, Behrouz Kamalvandi, Spokesperson for the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran (Farsi)-(00:25 - 01:09): "What I can say is that the nuclear industry has its roots in Iran, and it is not an industry that can be destroyed by strikes. Unfortunately, the enemy still has not understood this; they still lack such an understanding. However, we are certain that, in any case, this is an industry that contributes to various fields, such as health, medicine, agriculture, industry, and other sectors, all of which benefit the country. The Islamic Republic of Iran will certainly continue this path of progress with intensity and strength.""

"SOT3, Behrouz Kamalvandi, Spokesperson for the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran (Farsi)-(01:10 - 01:44): "There has always been a threat, which we have heard about many times. At the same time, what is certain is that we have always had, and will always have, the necessary foresight. We hope our enemies come to their senses and realize that the Islamic Republic of Iran will not, in fact, yield to force. They cannot achieve through force what they cannot obtain through negotiation.""

"SOT4, Behrouz Kamalvandi, Spokesperson for the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran (Farsi)-(01:45 - 02:13): "What is important is the rights and interests of the country, and we certainly pursue these through both paths, just as the country's officials have pointed out: the path of negotiation and the path of resistance. Neither contradicts the other. At the negotiating table, too, what the Islamic Republic of Iran wants is an emphasis on its own rights, and no one is permitted to waive these rights.""

"SOT5, Behrouz Kamalvandi, Spokesperson for the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran (Farsi)-(02:14 - 02:33): "The Islamic Republic of Iran will pursue the country's interests with authority and resolve. If these interests can be secured through diplomacy, so much the better; if not, we will certainly secure them with strength and might on the battlefield.

This security provides various social, moral, and public comfort dimensions in society, and such a valuable service, in addition to being a jihad in the way of God, possesses strong social support. The prominent role of FARAJA at various levels, from commanding and staff ranks to police stations and outposts, to ensure security has become more pronounced in recent years.”"

The focus and persistence of the criminal American-Zionist enemy to strike various levels of the Law Enforcement Forces (FARAJA) from the highest echelons to its frontline officers, demonstrated the importance of this institution more than ever. However, this desperate effort and the insidious attacks on the pillars of the system and societal security, for which there is no parallel in history, did not cause the brave forces of FARAJA to retreat even an inch from their mission; instead, they continued to fulfill the same roles and duties in the streets and vehicles that they performed in their headquarters.”"

"VO3, Seyyed Mojtaba Khamenei, Iran's Supreme Leader (Farsi) (01:49 - 02:47): "For this reason, the oppressed yet powerful nation of Iran is grateful for the tireless efforts and sacrifices of those serving the country's security; in turn, the law enforcement forces, which, like the Army and the IRGC; emerge from the depths of society, can enhance public trust in this valuable institution through trust-building behavior. At times, the hard work and sacrifices of security guardians may be taken for granted by some individuals, and it is precisely this sense of being wronged and unrecognized that increases their reward in the eyes of God. title: Iran Central Bank Governor Says Economy Won't Collapse Under U.S. Pressure; Vows to Turn U.S. Economic War Back on U.S.
text:
Iran Central Bank Governor Says Economy Won't Collapse Under U.S. Pressure; Vows to Turn U.S. Economic War Back on U.S."

"🔆🔅TEHRAN - October 7 - Abdolnaser Hemmati, Iran's Central Bank Governor, late last night, October 6th, made some remarks during a televised interview."

""
"SOT1, Abdolnaser Hemmati, Iran's Central Bank Governor: "I have a message for the U.S. Treasury Secretary and other U.S. officials: only five days remain in the two-week deadline they [the United States] gave, saying that the country’s [Iran's] economy was going to collapse. And here we are, discussing the country’s economic achievements, and I am telling them that this will not happen.""

"SOT2, Abdolnaser Hemmati, Iran's Central Bank Governor: "The U.S. government is a ruthless government. You can see how they martyred our children in [the southern Iranian city of] Minab, how they martyred our beloved Leader, and many others [during the war]. They [the Americans] were supposed to bring Iran to the point of collapse within two weeks [as a result of the war], achieve victory, and leave. They have now been at it for nine months. Then, 10 days ago, they announced that they wanted Iran to collapse economically within two weeks. Ten days have now passed since that announcement. And now, at the front line of the economic war, we will give them the same response, meaning that they will get the same result [and face economic collapse].""

"SOT3, Abdolnaser Hemmati, Iran's Central Bank Governor: "Now, in the economic war, just as they [the Americans] kept saying [during the military war] that 90 percent of their [Iranians'] missiles had been used up and so on, only to see more and more missiles raining down on them, the same thing is happening now [in the case of the economic war]. They keep saying that Iran’s foreign exchange reserves are running out, its revenues are drying up, and then they see that nothing has happened [to Iran]. Ultimately, they apply psychological pressure, engage in propaganda, and put pressure on the governments of regional countries. They are using all these measures to apply pressure and, in any case, break the Iranian economy. I assure the people that the Iranian economy will not be broken by these measures.""

"SOT4, Abdolnaser Hemmati, Iran's Central Bank Governor: "From the beginning of the year until roughly the middle of [the month of] Mehr [on the Iranian calendar (corresponding to October 7)], we have provided $24.9 billion in foreign currency. That is a significant amount; we have provided nearly $25 billion in foreign currency for the country, meaning that goods worth that amount have been imported into the country. The $25 billion compares with $28 billion during the same period last year, that is, from the beginning of last year up to this date. So, [in comparison] we have [only] had a 12-percent decrease in the provision of foreign currency.

text:
🔆🔅 TEHRAN, October 3rd — Ali Khezrian, a member of the Iranian Parliament's National Security Commission, made remarks."

"SOT1, Ali Khezrian, Member of Iranian Parliament's National Security Commission: "The enemy's assessment is that within the next two weeks it could first undermine our resilience on other fronts. The Zionist regime is seeking this, and the Americans are seeking this — to trigger an internal uprising in our country. As a member of the National Security Commission, I state that our security, intelligence, and law enforcement agencies are fully aware of this issue and have made arrests in this regard; they will not allow anyone to take action in the streets against this important achievement of the third imposed war in a way that violates national security.""

"SOT2, "A week ago, the U.S. Treasury Secretary said that the Iranian economy would collapse within the next two weeks. Well, a week has passed. If our officials act correctly, including on the foreign-exchange issue, and if there is no dumping of currency into non-essential goods — if they can properly implement these currency controls in the Iranian economy — then even this past week, and even these economic fluctuations, are due to that psychological warfare, not to any real impact on the ground. Therefore, we believe that the current conditions are not heading toward an economic collapse.""

"SOT3, "Zionists are seeking to involve the Americans in a military conflict; the Zionist lobby is active in this matter, as are those around Trump. Trump has lost a war and does not want to exit under these circumstances. The path is completely clear. The Islamic Republic of Iran has announced certain conditions; these conditions must be met so they can leave here with dignity. The Islamic Republic of Iran will not create a window for a dignified exit for anyone under these circumstances unless our national interests are secured.""

"SOT4, "In many sectors of food production, under the guidance of our martyred Imam [Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei], we are producers rather than importers, and we are capable of meeting our own needs. Therefore, our resilience regarding essential commodities is in a completely favorable condition. According to reports from the government and the Minister of Agriculture, the country's foreign-exchange situation is also favorable; we have been able to sell our oil, and we continue to do so.""

"SOT5, "The enemy's miscalculation, plus actions by the Zionist regime, could provide grounds for a confrontation, which we have also predicted. In this regard, our country will not face problems with resilience; our people should know this. Our dear country and officials have made plans such that if they want to start this war — which is what we predict they will do, as their regional posture tells us — it is not secret news that they are doing this. Under these circumstances, resilience for our country will not be a problem.

" "
"SOT1, Ali Balali, Senior advisor to the commander of the IRGC Aerospace Force (Farsi)-(00:00 - 00:43): "We build all the facilities we need in the missile sector ourselves, and we are capable of exporting them. In drones, air defense, and space—these are areas where we started, and using the experience we gained, we have made progress. We have reached a point where, in the drone sector, the United States has copied our Shahed-136. This demonstrates the level of determination and will behind this achievement; those who possess all the think tanks, research, and development centers could not build it themselves and are instead copying from us.""

"SOT2, Ali Balali, Senior advisor to the commander of the IRGC Aerospace Force (Farsi)-(00:44 - 01:14): "We have made progress in the missile field in sectors that involve the latest global technologies. The nozzles used for our missiles are made of carbon fiber and can withstand temperatures of 3,000 degrees and pressures of 100 atmospheres. Who built these? Our own scientists, our own students—individuals who worked in this country, studied, and had the belief and confidence in themselves that they could do it, and so they did.""

"SOT3, Ali Balali, Senior advisor to the commander of the IRGC Aerospace Force (Farsi)-(01:15 - 02:08): "We do not really rest; we are always striving and meeting our own needs in the aerospace field. Thankfully, there is continuity among the components related to this work, and it is occurring across all the sectors we require. We are grateful that we have been able to maintain this steadfastness so far, and there is no cause for concern. What you are seeing now is that the Americans are raising concerns about their reserves of interceptor missiles and the like, and they are truly at a loss as to what to do. However, we are not in that situation, and thank God, we can continue this battle for as long as necessary, given the capabilities being developed by our Ministry of Defense and other sectors.

title: A Return to the Classroom
text:
A Return to the Classroom"

"Tehran - September 21 - President Masoud Pezeshkian inaugurated Iran’s new academic year on Tuesday by ringing the ceremonial school bell at a girls’ school in Tehran’s District 18 (Yaftabad neighborhood), marking a pivotal moment for a nation emerging from an extended period of remote education. "

"This academic year carries particular significance, as it represents Iran’s full-scale return to in-person instruction following months of nationwide school closures that had forced approximately 16.6 million students across 117,140 schools into virtual learning. The prolonged shift to online education had placed immense strain on families, particularly working parents with young children, and raised concerns about learning loss and educational equity."

"Education Minister Kazemi had previously emphasized the government’s determination to restore classroom instruction, stating: “Even under the most difficult conditions, we will firmly continue with in-person classes”. The return to physical classrooms has been described by officials as a critical step toward educational recovery and normalization."

" International Engagement Ahead"

"Following the school ceremony, President Pezeshkian is scheduled to depart Tehran’s Mehrabad Airport for New York to participate in the United Nations General Assembly, underscoring Iran’s continued engagement on the international stage.

title: Pezeshkian's India Trip: Iran Looks to BRICS to Counter Isolation and Boost Ties
text:
Pezeshkian's India Trip: Iran Looks to BRICS to Counter Isolation and Boost Ties"

"Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian visited New Delhi in September 2026 for the 18th BRICS Summit. It was his first trip to India as president, and the visit was marked by significant diplomatic engagement."

" 🎥 What Happened During the Trip"

"**A Warm Diplomatic Welcome**"
"Prime Minister Narendra Modi mounted a notably warm public outreach. The most striking moment was a photograph from the BRICS Business Forum showing Modi walking **hand-in-hand** with President Pezeshkian, with Russian President Vladimir Putin and South African President Cyril Ramaphosa alongside them. This image was widely interpreted as a symbol of India's strategic autonomy and its ability to engage with Iran and Russia while maintaining ties with Western powers."

"**Bilateral Talks with PM Modi**"
"Pezeshkian and Modi held bilateral talks—their second meeting in under two weeks, following a meeting in Bishkek on August 31. Key topics included:"
"*  **Strategic Agreements**: Pezeshkian called for the continuation of long-standing strategic agreements with India."
"*  **West Asia Situation**: The leaders discussed the prevailing regional situation, with Modi reiterating India's commitment to "enduring peace"."
"*  **Energy Security**: Modi raised the safety of seafarers amid disruptions in the strategic Strait of Hormuz."
"*  **Trade**: Modi emphasized the need to move forward with a "long-term and win-win strategy" for India-Iran friendship."

"**Meeting with the President of India**"
"President Pezeshkian was the **only dignitary hosted by Rashtrapati Bhavan** during the summit. He met with President Droupadi Murmu, who expressed appreciation for Tehran's support of India's BRICS presidency and discussed the strong cultural and people-to-people ties between the nations."

"**Other Engagements**"
"Pezeshkian was accompanied by his daughter, **Zahra Pezeshkian**, who was escorted by Union Minister Annpurna Devi to the BRICS Bazaar at the Crafts Museum. The visit also served as a platform for Iran to strengthen ties with other BRICS members, including China and Russia, amid geopolitical pressure.

"SOT1, Mohammad Soleimani, Head of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Office in Hormozgan province (Farsi)-(00:03 - 00:47): "It was around early August when the families and the Bandar Lengeh governor's office informed us and requested that we inquire about the disappearance of these dear individuals. Based on previous experience and cases, we notified Iran's missions in Dubai and Abu Dhabi, and they prepared a memorandum that was submitted to the Emirati government. Fortunately, it happened very quickly; about two weeks ago, they provided us with the names of 10 people who are in an Abu Dhabi prison and will be released soon.""

"SOT2, Mohammad Soleimani, Head of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Office in Hormozgan province (Farsi)-(00:54 - 01:21): "Our consulate in Dubai arranged tickets for them to arrive in Bandar Abbas on September 7, but unfortunately, due to problems on the part of the UAE government, they did not agree and the flight was canceled. However, a flight was arranged from Dubai to Tehran yesterday and they arrived in Tehran, and they will arrive in Bandar Abbas today.""

"SOT3, Mohammad Soleimani, Head of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Office in Hormozgan province (Farsi)-(01:35 - 01:55): "We inquired about 13 people in total, but the UAE government reported 10 to us; they said three are not there. title: **Why is the U.S. pursuing such a system?**
text:
"**Why is the U.S. pursuing such a system?**"

"Subsurface warfare is one of the most complex areas of military operations. The underwater environment, unlike the sky and the earth's surface, limits the possibility of constant and easy communication, and detecting a subsurface vehicle is far more difficult. For this reason, the use of unmanned systems can reduce some of these limitations. An autonomous vehicle can remain in a specific area for a long time, collect information, and carry out its mission without putting crew members' lives at risk. The Dive-LD is fundamentally designed for exactly this purpose."

"**The significance of the capture**"

"The IRGC's statement specifically mentions "intelligence and operational dominance." This phrase carries special meaning in subsurface operations. Detecting and intercepting an unmanned underwater vehicle—especially a system designed for independent operations—requires a set of intelligence, reconnaissance, and subsurface environmental monitoring capabilities."

"The Dive-LD incident should not be viewed merely as a one-off operation. The main significance of this event lies in the fact that it shows the future of warfare will not be solely about missiles and manned aircraft; a significant portion of military competition will shift to underwater environments, autonomous systems, artificial intelligence, sensors, and electronic warfare. In modern warfare, sometimes the most valuable victory is not the destruction of a system, but its discovery, control, and acquisition—because in the latter case, the enemy not only loses an operational tool but also exposes some of its technological secrets to study.

title: Gulf Allies Lose Faith in Trump as Iran War Drags On, Report Says
text:
Gulf Allies Lose Faith in Trump as Iran War Drags On, Report Says"

""

"Excerpt from Trump's Meeting with a Regional Ally"

"Gulf leaders are growing increasingly frustrated with the Trump administration's handling of the war with Iran, fearing that Washington lacks the diplomatic capability to secure a peace deal, according to a new report by The Washington Post."

"The report, cited by multiple Iranian media outlets, reveals that Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait, and Bahrain have reached a shared concern over U.S. policy after months of conflict and continued Iranian missile and drone strikes."

"**"Trump started this war, and we are paying the price,"** a Gulf official told The Washington Post on condition of anonymity. According to the official, Arab anger toward the United States has now reached its highest level since the joint U.S.-Israeli attack on Iran in February."

"The frustration stems from Trump's contradictory approach—repeatedly threatening Iran with renewed strikes while simultaneously backing off and touting progress in negotiations. This inconsistency has led some Gulf countries to question whether hosting large U.S. military bases on their soil remains worthwhile."

"**"From the very beginning, there was dissatisfaction,"** said Firas Mqsd, Director of the Middle East and North Africa at the Eurasia Group. He noted that America's Gulf allies feel they have been **"dragged into a war for no reason"** —one that Trump is now struggling to end. Trump's Iran policy, he added, is often described in the region as **"unstable"** and **"unpredictable"**."

"**Trust in the United States has declined since the war began,** said Anna Jacobs, a researcher at the Arab Gulf States Institute in Washington. She added that U.S. allies believe Washington's actions have made them **"less secure, not more secure"**."

"While Gulf states still rely on the U.S. as their primary security partner and arms supplier, some are exploring alternatives. A recent mutual defense agreement among Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan was interpreted by a senior European official as **"a message to America"** —signaling that three powerful Sunni nations are **"trying to diversify their security and defense partnerships"** because **"America alone is no longer enough"**."

"The White House pushed back, insisting that Trump has **"excellent relationships with all our Gulf partners"** and that the U.S. has been in regular contact with regional allies."

"But analysts say the shift is real. The economic pressure from the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure, and the prolonged war have all deepened Gulf anxieties. Arab officials who once hoped for a quick end to the conflict are now demanding a resolution as soon as possible."

"Based on reporting from The Washington Post, as cited by Euronews Persian and Tasnim News Agency

title: **Iran Accelerates Repairs on Hormozgan Bridges Destroyed by US Airstrikes, Key Routes to Reopen by Late September**
text:
"**Iran Accelerates Repairs on Hormozgan Bridges Destroyed by US Airstrikes, Key Routes to Reopen by Late September**"

"**BANDAR ABBAS, Iran** – Iranian road authorities have announced significant progress in rebuilding at least six strategic bridges in the southern province of Hormozgan that were destroyed during US airstrikes in mid-July, with officials confirming that major routes will be reopened to traffic within days."

"The attacks, which occurred on the night of July 16-17, marked the sixth consecutive night of American military strikes against Iranian territory. The US Central Command (CENTCOM) said the operations targeted military infrastructure, including coastal surveillance sites, air defense systems, and military logistics routes. However, the strikes hit multiple bridges in Bandar Khamir County, killing at least seven people and wounding several others, according to local authorities and state media, which later revised the death toll to eight."

"Among the damaged structures were the Geriveh (Gachin) Bridge, the Latidan (Kalmatli) Bridge, and the Kahurestan Bridge—a critical artery linking the major port city of Bandar Abbas to Shiraz and the interior Fars province. The Kahurestan crossing is particularly vital for commercial shipping and passenger transport, as Bandar Abbas sits on the strategic Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly one-fifth of the world's oil passes. Other bridges hit included two crossings on the Kahurestan-Lar road, a semi-finished bridge on the Bandar Khamir-Kashar axis, and a bridge near Maru village."

"In a statement to local media, Hormozgan's Road Administration provided a detailed update on the reconstruction effort. "The large Gachin bridge has been fully installed, and we are currently laying asphalt on its surface," an official said. "The Kahurestan bridge is also practically finished and will be reopened to traffic within this week.""

"Regarding the remaining damaged bridges, where traffic is currently being diverted through temporary side passages, authorities assured that all reconstruction work will be finalized by the end of Shahrivar, which corresponds to late September. The rapid repair timeline underscores the strategic importance of these road networks, as Iran moves to restore normalcy in the region following the extensive military campaign.

title: **Three Iranian Soldiers Return Home After Six Months in Captivity**
text:
**Three Iranian Soldiers Return Home After Six Months in Captivity**"

"On August 28th, After six months of separation and captivity, three young soldiers from the Iranian Army who served on the naval vessel IRIS Lavan have returned to their hometown of Darab in Fars Province. They were welcomed back by their families, friends, local residents, and officials."

"**Background on the IRIS Lavan Incident**"

"The IRIS Lavan is a *Hengam*-class landing ship of Iran's naval forces, named after Lavan Island."

"The vessel was part of Iran's naval contingent participating in India's International Fleet Review and the MILAN 2026 multinational naval exercise in Visakhapatnam in February 2026. On March 4, 2026, the IRIS Lavan docked at the Port of Kochi in southern India after experiencing serious technical malfunctions. This occurred on the same day that the Iranian frigate IRIS Dena was struck and sunk by a US submarine in the Indian Ocean."

"India granted the IRIS Lavan permission to dock on "humanitarian grounds", and its 183 crew members were accommodated at Indian naval facilities in Kochi. Subsequently, India repatriated the non-essential crew members of the vessel. However, it appears that three of the crew members were held in captivity during this period."

"**Note on the return:** The three soldiers returned to Darab on August 28 (approximately 17 hours prior to the time of this report). A welcome ceremony was held for them at the Pir Morad Martyrs' Cemetery in Darab, where they were reunited with their families and received by local officials and community members.

title: **Iran Fuel Crisis Deepens as US Sanctions, War Damage, and Panic Buying Trigger Massive Petrol Queues**
text:
**Iran Fuel Crisis Deepens as US Sanctions, War Damage, and Panic Buying Trigger Massive Petrol Queues**"

"By Iman Keyhanfard"

"**Tehran, August 27, 2026** — Long queues have formed at petrol stations across Tehran and several other Iranian cities as fuel shortages, supply disruptions, and widespread panic among motorists intensify. Drivers are reportedly waiting up to two hours in lines that snake around filling stations, while some pumps have shut down entirely after running out of fuel."

"Panic buying has compounded the supply crunch. Drivers are filling up tanks before they are even half empty, driven by fears of imminent price hikes and quota reductions. State-run *Hamshahri* newspaper reported that much of the recent queueing stems not from actual shortages but from "precautionary demand" fueled by anxiety over future fuel policy. Those fears were stoked after Mohsen Haji-Mirzaei, the president's chief of staff, announced that petrol quotas would be reviewed and that consumers would likely pay higher prices for usage beyond their allocated limits."

"Despite authorities distributing a record 26 million litres of petrol in Tehran on Monday — about 30 per cent above the daily average — queues have only grown longer as demand surges. The National Iranian Oil Refining and Distribution Company has denied any nationwide fuel shortage, but reports from provinces including Kerman, Mashhad, Mazandaran, Gilan, Hormozgan, and Fars indicate similar disruptions."

"The issue carries deep political sensitivity. Past efforts to raise petrol prices — most notably in November 2019 — triggered deadly nationwide protests. With Iran's currency plunging to a new low of 2 million rials to the dollar and year-on-year inflation approaching 90 per cent, any further price hikes could stoke renewed public anger."

"In a late-night TV interview on August 21, Iranian Defense Ministry spokesman General Reza Talaei-Nik stated that national power is the key strategy for preserving Iran's independence and security. He said Iran's defense production has doubled over the past year (July 2025–July 2026) following the "12-day war," with some strategic items seeing a threefold increase during active conflict. He emphasized synchronization of production with battlefield consumption, and announced that Iran has stopped monthly public unveilings of new weapons to protect operational secrecy. Talaei-Nik also claimed Iran ranks among the world's top ten countries in missile technology and among the top nations in drone production, with over 1,000 advanced indigenous systems now being manufactured domestically. He dismissed recent threats from Trump and Netanyahu, framing Iran's military growth as a response to "hybrid" threats combining military and non-military fronts."

text:
Iranian Parliamentary Delegation Presents Gift to Iraqi Speaker Mohammad al-Halbousi"

"**Baghdad, Iraq –** A high-ranking parliamentary delegation from the Islamic Republic of Iran, led by Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, presented a gift to Iraqi Parliament Speaker Mohammad al-Halbousi during an official visit to Baghdad."

"The Iranian delegation arrived in the Iraqi capital on Wednesday for a three-day visit aimed at discussing bilateral cooperation, border security, counter-terrorism efforts, and economic relations. Upon arrival at Baghdad International Airport, the delegation was received by First Deputy Speaker of the Iraqi Parliament Adnan Fayhan."

"Later, at the parliament headquarters, Speaker al-Halbousi officially welcomed Speaker Qalibaf and the accompanying delegation. During the meeting, the Iranian side presented a gift to the Iraqi speaker as a gesture of goodwill and friendship between the two nations."

"Speaking before departing Tehran, Qalibaf described the visit as particularly significant, emphasizing that relations between Baghdad and Tehran are "highly important and fundamental to regional developments". He noted that the two sides would discuss major issues concerning the development of economic, political, cultural, social and security relations between Iran and Iraq."

"Qalibaf also highlighted what he described as the effective roles played by both countries in regional affairs, stating that the visit could help lay the groundwork for taking advantage of new opportunities facing the two nations."

"The visit comes as part of ongoing efforts to strengthen parliamentary and diplomatic ties between the Islamic Republic of Iran and the Republic of Iraq.

title: Lake Urmia Islands Welcome Birds Once Again
text:
Lake Urmia Islands Welcome Birds Once Again"

"The islands of Lake Urmia in northwestern Iran have once again become hosts to migratory birds. This marks a hopeful ecological revival for the lake, which had dramatically shrunk over the past two decades due to severe drought, dam construction, and water diversion—losing nearly 90% of its surface area at its worst point."

"However, increased rainfall over recent years, combined with water release projects, has raised the lake's water levels and reduced its salinity, allowing its islands to transform back into safe nesting and resting grounds. The returning flocks include species such as flamingos, pelicans, and various migratory waterfowl, signaling a partial but significant recovery for this UNESCO-listed biosphere reserve. "

"🎦 Video footage shows the vibrant return of these bird populations to the region.

title: Footage from the start of the funeral ceremony for Iraj Khajeh Amiri, attended by a diverse crowd of people and figures from the arts and culture, in front of Tehran's Vahdat Hall.
text:
Footage from the start of the funeral ceremony for Iraj Khajeh Amiri, attended by a diverse crowd of people and figures from the arts and culture, in front of Tehran's Vahdat Hall."

""

"**Who was Iraj Khajeh Amiri?**"

"Iraj Khajeh Amiri (born Hossein Khajeh Amiri Khaledi, 1933–2026) was one of Iran’s most beloved and respected classical singers. He was widely known by his stage name, **Iraj**, and was affectionately nicknamed **"Pahlavan-e Avaz"** (Champion of Song)."

"Born into a musical family in Khaled Abad, near Kashan, he began studying traditional Persian singing (*avaz*) under his father at the age of six. Over a career spanning more than seven decades, he became a towering figure in Iranian classical music, often mentioned alongside legends like Mohammad-Reza Shajarian."

"Beyond his singing, Iraj was also a retired army officer and performed in many Iranian films before the 1979 Islamic Revolution. After the revolution, he stopped appearing in movies but continued his musical career and teaching, founding a music school in Tehran. His son, Ehsan Khajeh Amiri, is also a well-known Iranian pop singer."

"Iraj passed away on August 12, 2026, at the age of 94. His funeral ceremony, held at Tehran’s Vahdat Hall, drew a large crowd of ordinary citizens as well as artists, musicians, and cultural figures—a testament to his enduring legacy as one of the great voices of Persian traditional music.

"Informed Sources Deny Alleged Plan to Reopen Strait of Hormuz"

"Some media outlets had claimed that the Islamic Republic of Iran had agreed to a plan for reopening the Strait of Hormuz. However, informed sources have rejected these allegations, emphasizing that no change has been made in Iran's policy regarding this strategic waterway."

"A source close to Iran's negotiating team, speaking to Fars News Agency's political correspondent, denied the reports about Iran agreeing to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, stating: *"The Islamic Republic of Iran has not reached any agreement on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, and the news published in this regard is false."*"

"Meanwhile, a follow-up inquiry by a Fars reporter from a military informed source also indicated that the claim is untrue and entirely denied."

"This military source rejected the published reports, stressing: *"As long as America's hostile actions and provocations continue, the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed. Transit will only be possible through the designated route, in coordination with the IRGC Navy and after obtaining a permit to cross the strait. Otherwise, other routes are unsafe, and any vessels attempting to traverse them will certainly face incidents."*"

"The informed source further emphasized that the claims regarding Iran's agreement to any plan for reopening the Strait of Hormuz are baseless, and that no decision or change has been made in the Islamic Republic of Iran's policies concerning this strategic waterway."

"Hours earlier, some media, citing Israeli journalist Barak Ravid, had published reports claiming that Iran had agreed to a plan for reopening the Strait of Hormuz—under which ships would enter the Persian Gulf through Iranian territorial waters and exit through Omani territorial waters.

title: IRAN'S FALLEN EAGLE RETURNS HOME: MARTYR PILOT WHO STRUCK US BASE IN DARING SU-24 MISSION
text:
IRAN'S FALLEN EAGLE RETURNS HOME: MARTYR PILOT WHO STRUCK US BASE IN DARING SU-24 MISSION"

"**SHIRAZ, Iran** – The body of Second Brigadier General Majid Kazemi, the Su-24 fighter pilot who led a daring retaliatory strike against a major US military installation, arrived in his hometown of Shiraz on Thursday as thousands gathered to honor the fallen hero."

"The funeral procession began at Shahid Doran Air Base, with senior military officials and comrades paying tribute to the pilot whose identity was only confirmed this week through DNA testing after months of uncertainty. His body will be carried through Imam Hossein Square on Friday following weekly prayers, as the people of Shiraz prepare to bid a final farewell to one of their own."

"**A Mission of Retaliation**"

"On March 2, Kazemi was among the pilots of two Iranian Air Force Su-24 bombers that took off from Shahid Doran Air Base in response to what Iran described as "savage and treacherous attacks" by US and Israeli forces. The operation followed a large-scale US-Israeli military campaign against Iran that began on February 28 after the assassination of then-Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and several senior commanders."

"**Penetrating Advanced Defenses**"

"The Iranian Army statement detailed how Kazemi and his fellow pilots penetrated the enemy's advanced surveillance systems and multiple radar positions before carrying out a bombing raid on the US-operated Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar. The strike caused heavy damage to the facility. Iran's retaliatory operations ultimately included 100 waves of attacks against American and Israeli positions across the region."

"**A Hero's Final Flight**"

"While returning from the mission, the two Su-24 aircraft were struck by enemy air defense systems over the Persian Gulf. Kazemi was martyred alongside three crewmates, whose fate remains unknown as search efforts continue."

"Army Chief praised Kazemi as a "true hero" who embodied a generation of warriors who pledged to become the shield of their nation's skies. His body was transferred from Shahid Lashgari Air Base in Tehran before arriving in Shiraz for burial."

""Martyrdom is not the end of a great man's journey; it is the beginning of his immortality," read a tribute published by Tehran Times. "Nations endure because of men like him.

title: 📹 Arbaeen banquet table designed like an Iranian ballistic missile in Samawah, Iraq.
text:
"📹 Arbaeen banquet table designed like an Iranian ballistic missile in Samawah, Iraq."

"🔺Along the Arbaeen pilgrimage route, one of the service Mowkebs (hospitality tents) in the city of Samawah, Iraq, has built its reception/dining area with a design resembling an Iranian ballistic missile."

""
"The Arbaeen pilgrimage marks the 40th day of mourning for Imam Hussein (the grandson of the Prophet Muhammad) and is one of the world's largest annual religious gatherings, attracting over 20 million Shia Muslims—most of whom travel from Iran—to the holy city of Karbala in Iraq. "

"Along the routes leading to Karbala, local Iraqis set up thousands of "Mowkebs" (volunteer-run service stations) that offer free food, drinks, medical aid, and resting places to pilgrims as an act of religious hospitality and charity. Samawah is a key transit city in southern Iraq on the main overland route towards Karbala."

"This particular Mowkeb's choice to shape its food-serving area like an Iranian ballistic missile is a striking and highly symbolic visual gesture. While it showcases the hosts' creative and competitive spirit in decorating their tents to attract attention, it also reflects the deep cultural, political, and religious solidarity between Iran and Iraq within this specific context. For many participants, the missile design is viewed as a display of shared strength and resistance, while for others, it highlights how even religious hospitality can be intertwined with regional geopolitical symbolism in the Middle East.
